Subject: AWS Marketplace metering integration — initial info request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo — Acme Cloud is excited to move Redwood onto the AWS Marketplace catalog. Procurement wants to understand how metering and fulfillment will work with our SaaS contract: specifically entitlement mapping, how MPIDs are used, and the expected billing flow so they can confirm internal finance approvals.

A few concrete questions to start:
- What does Redwood need from us (MPID, account mapping, role permissions) to enable metering calls?
- Is there an expected window for the first metering event after a user signs up via Marketplace (any latency concerns)?
- Do you support both by-seat licensing and subscription tiers via the metering API or do we need to model that in our own entitlement layer?

We have our procurement lead cc'd (Susan). Can we set a short working session next week to align on the technical and contractual pieces?

Cheers,
Chris

Hi Chris — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list. Happy to run a 30-min sync next week. Tentatively proposing Tue 6/17 10:00am PT — does that work for you?

Quick answers to the bullets so procurement has something concrete before the call:
- What we need: MPID (the marketplace product id), the AWS account id(s) you want tied to the entitlement mapping, and a technical contact who can approve the IAM role we’ll use for fulfillment/test calls.
- Metering latency: typical metering API calls are near-real-time (seconds), but we recommend a 5–10 minute reconciliation window for first-customer billing to account for propagation and retries.
- Licensing models: Redwood supports SKU-level metering through the Marketplace Metering (usage) APIs; for by-seat licensing we recommend modeling seats as a SKU + quantity reporting. If you want tiered pricing with different SKUs per tier, that’s straightforward to map as separate SKUs and entitlements.

I’ve attached our onboarding checklist to this thread (RDW_AWS_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf). Soojin + Karthik — can you confirm the technical pre-reqs and whether we need a sandbox MPID before production?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering integration — initial info request (technical notes)

Marissa / Karthik / Chris — adding some technical notes ahead of our sync. High level steps we’ll run with Acme:

1) MPID & Entitlement mapping
   - We need the AWS MPID for the SaaS listing and the exact AWS Account IDs (or org units) to associate to entitlements if you prefer account-scoped purchases.
2) Fulfillment URL and contract handshake
   - For SaaS contracts we implement AWS SaaS Fulfillment (PostPurchase) flow. We validate the signature from AWS, create (or update) our internal entitlement record, and issue a customer account with the correct SKU/quantity.
3) Metering calls
   - Metering API: we will call Marketplace Metering.registerUsage for usage-based metering, or PutEntitlements for entitlement-based grants depending on model.
   - Recommendation: for seat-based products, report seats as quantity on registerUsage and send a daily reconciliation job to prevent drift.
4) Testing & sandbox
   - AWS provides a sandbox MPID; we can run an end-to-end simulation there before prod.

I’ve attached a short markdown with the implementation checklist (metering_integration_steps.md). Key engineering asks from Acme: provide MPID (prod+sandbox if available), IAM principal for test webhook validation, and a sample customer account id mapping strategy.

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachment: metering_integration_steps.md

From: Marketplace Partner Engineer <mp-engineer@amazon.com>

Subject: AWS SaaS fulfillment & metering — guidance and next steps

Hi all,

Thanks for the work so far — a couple of notes from the AWS side to speed integration:

- Fulfillment flow: use the AWS SaaS Fulfillment URL (we provided in the partner portal) to accept PostPurchase notifications. Make sure your endpoint validates the x-amzn-sns-message-type and signature.
- MPID mapping: create a mapping table in your DB keyed by awsAccountId+mpId so you can support purchases across multiple accounts.
- Testing: request a sandbox MPID via the partner portal and use the test buyer flows; we can generate a sample order for you.
- Billing reconciliation: set up a daily report that compares registerUsage events with your internal entitlements; handle failed registerUsage retries to avoid underbilling.

Attached is the AWS SaaS Fulfillment guide (aws-saas-fulfillment-guide.pdf) and a short checklist.

If you want, we can provision a sandbox MPID today — tell me the partner account id.

Best,
Alex Porter
